ai.description: The Cave Racer grows up to 2.5 meters. It is olive-green or grey with a distinctive black lateral stripe and a dark post-ocular streak. A dorsal ladder-like pattern often fades toward the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Elaphe taeniura* is the distinct, bold black stripe extending horizontally from behind each eye, contrasting with its patterned body.
ai.habitat: The Cave Racer inhabits dense tropical evergreen and broadleaf forests, typically ranging from lowlands up to 2,000 meters in elevation across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Cave Racer is a skilled climber that frequently hunts bats in total darkness, navigating cave ceilings with remarkable agility to snatch prey mid-flight.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Elaphe taeniura* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs from spring to early summer, with hatching following an incubation of 60–80 days.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Elaphe taeniura* is found in Northeast India, specifically across Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Nagaland, ranging from lowlands to 2,000m.
